label: Global well posedness of MS
title: Theorem
body_md:
\textup{(\cite{NakamuraWada2007}, Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 1.2)} \label{Global well posedness of MS}
Suppose that $(\psi^{\mathrm{in}}_{\hbar},A^{\mathrm{in}}_{0,\hbar},A^{\mathrm{in}}_{1,\hbar})\in H^{4}(\mathbb{R}^{3})\times H^{4}(\mathbb{R}^{3})\times H^{3}(\mathbb{R}^{3})$ satisfies \eqref{MS initial data}. Then there exists a unique solution $(\psi_{\hbar},A_{\hbar})\in C(\mathbb{R};H^{4}(\mathbb{R}^{3}))\times C(\mathbb{R};H^{4}(\mathbb{R}^{3}))$ to the Cauchy problem \eqref{Maxwell Schrodinger eq}-\eqref{MS initial data}. Moreover, $\partial_{t}A_{\hbar}\in C(\mathbb{R};H^{3}(\mathbb{R}^{3}))$.

label: local existence of solution
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{local existence of solution}
Suppose that $\rho^{\mathrm{in}}\in H^{s-1}(\mathbb{R}^{3})$ and
$(u^{\mathrm{in}},E^{\mathrm{in}},B^
{\mathrm{in}})\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{3})$ satisfy \eqref{EMI} for some $s>\frac{5}{2}$ and suppose that $\left\Vert u^{\mathrm{in}}\right\Vert_{\infty}<1 $.  Then, there exist some $T>0$ and a solution $(\rho,u,E,B)$  to \eqref{Euler Maxwell} with initial data 
$(\rho^{\mathrm{in}},u^{\mathrm{in }},E^{\mathrm{in}},B^{\mathrm{in}})$. Moreover, it holds that $\rho\in C([0,T];H^{s-1}(\mathbb{R}^{3}))$ and  $(u,E,B)\in C([0,T];H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{3}))$ with the bound $\left\Vert u\right\Vert_{L^{\infty}([0,T];L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{3}))} <1$.
